question: In Young’s double-slit experiment, blue light is replaced by red light while keeping the slit separation and screen distance unchanged. How will the fringe width change? Justify your answer.

options.A: The fringe width increases because red light has a longer wavelength than blue light, and fringe width is directly proportional to wavelength ($\beta \propto \lambda$).
options.B: The fringe width decreases because red light has a higher frequency and shorter wavelength than blue light.
options.C: The fringe width stays exactly the same because it depends only on screen distance and slit separation.
options.D: The fringes merge into a single solid blue band because red light cannot undergo interference.
